## What is the paper trying to do?

<br>

::: {.callout-note title="**What did we learn about these conflicts?**" icon="false"}
- What are the scope conditions?
- Where do Iraq and Afghanistan sit in the universe of cases?
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note title="**What kind of theoretical and empirical world emerges from this literature?**" icon="false"}
- The paper describes the literature but not the world it depicts
- How does the corpus differ in comparison to what "actually" happened?
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note title="**Was the work useful to policy makers?**" icon="false"}
- Policy reports and briefings
- Journal publication dates ≠ when research reached policymakers
:::

## Research Design

<br>

::: {.callout-note title="**Descriptive claim**: quantitative research on Iraq and Afghanistan focuses on micro-level phenomena and rarely observes the internal workings of insurgents or governing elites" icon="false"}
- How much of this results from selection process?

- Excluding qualitative work and books makes insurgents and elites look invisible

- Excluding cross-national studies makes the literature look more micro

  - Over-sampling from Q1 journals may compound this
:::

::: {.callout-note title="**Comparative claim**: these quantitative studies failed to accurately capture the complexity and fluidity within these cases (in comparison to qualitative work)" icon="false"}
- Largely untested
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Suggestion" icon="false"}
- Collect a similar dataset of qualitative studies of Iraq and Afghanistan over the same period and compare findings
:::

## Time and Context

<br>

::: {.callout-note title="Heterogeneity across time and cases" icon="false"}
- Each conflict lasts for almost two decades and goes through different phases

  - E.g. American occupation and Sunni insurgency (2003-2011) vs anti-ISIS air campaign (2014-2017)

- Are Afghanistan and Iraq different in important ways?

  - E.g. Sectarian cleavage in Iraq

- Might the mixed and uncertain findings across the literature result from heterogeneity across phases and cases?
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-important title="Suggestion" icon="false"}
- Disaggregate papers by the period they study
- Compare findings between Iraq and Afghanistan
:::

## Using the Dataset

<br>

::: {.callout-important title="Suggestions" icon="false"}
- Code for funding source, institutional affiliation, data source, early vs late papers

- Consider weighting by citations to capture influence of a paper

- More descriptives and exploration of the data
:::
